name: Missive
tagline: Combine email with internal comments and assignments for a small team

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Up to 3 users; 15 days of email and chat history.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: Up to 5 users; unlimited history; up to 10 personal accounts and 5 shared accounts per user; no rules, integrations, analytics, API or AI.

tiers.name: Productive
tiers.limits: Up to 50 users; up to 1,000 rules; unlimited history; basic analytics, API, integrations and AI.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Unlimited users; up to 1,000 rules; unlimited history; advanced analytics, SAML SSO and IP restrictions.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Up to 3 users; 15 days of email and chat history
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (-20%); 30-day free trial, no card
pricing.hiddenCosts: Shared accounts are capped at 5 per user; each additional block of 5 shared accounts costs $15/month. Productive and Business AI can use prepaid Missive credits (accounts begin with $5) with a 25% markup over provider cost, or the customer's own API key; annual seats removed mid-term remain billed but can be reassigned.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Missive, combine email with internal comments and assignments for a small team. The hard boundary is real-time collaboration, many channels, rules, integrations, and shared-inbox reliability, plus mail infrastructure, integrations, and client polish.
coreLoopDIY: Connect an existing mailbox, index messages locally, combine email with internal comments and assignments for a small team, and send through the account's normal SMTP service.
whatYouLose: real-time collaboration, many channels, rules, integrations, and shared-inbox reliability
moatNotes: mail infrastructure, integrations, and client polish
ongoingBurden: IMAP quirks, OAuth, MIME, threading, search, attachments, offline sync, notifications, secure storage, and provider changes
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Missive because an email client can be rebuilt; operating a trusted mail service with excellent deliverability cannot. The recurring cost buys IMAP quirks, OAuth, MIME, threading, search, attachments, offline sync, notifications, secure storage, and provider changes, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: mailcow
priorArt.desc: Popular open-source mail-server suite that demonstrates the operational complexity of hosted mail.

alternatives.name: Chatwoot
alternatives.desc: Collaborative email with private notes, mentions and ownership; also handles chat when Missive was doing too much.

facts.install: Docker Compose on a Linux VM, followed by environment, database, reverse-proxy and TLS configuration
facts.dataFormat: Application data in PostgreSQL, queues/cache in Redis, and attachments on local disk or S3-compatible/cloud object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It handles ownership and private notes but loses Missive's chat-like email collaboration and broader team-communication polish.
facts.setupBlocker: Provisioning a Linux server and correctly wiring DNS/TLS, SMTP, PostgreSQL/Redis and storage

alternatives.name: Frappe Helpdesk
alternatives.desc: Assignments, comments and shared queues in a clean interface; the Frappe stack is the hidden teammate.

facts.install: Run Frappe's easy-install script against the stable container image on a Linux server
facts.dataFormat: Tickets in the Frappe site database, with public and private attachments in the site's files directories
facts.gapVsPaid: It turns collaborative email into a conventional support queue and adds a Frappe stack to maintain.
facts.setupBlocker: A Linux server, domain/DNS, Docker or the easy-install script, and mail account configuration

alternatives.name: FreeScout
alternatives.desc: Shared mailboxes, internal notes and assignments without seat fees; chat-style polish is traded for server care.

facts.install: Install on a PHP/MySQL host with its web installer, or deploy a community Docker image
facts.dataFormat: Mailboxes, users and conversation metadata in the configured SQL database, with attachments in application server storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Its shared-mailbox workflow is less fluid than Missive's chat-style collaboration, and advanced modules plus server care add friction.
facts.setupBlocker: A web server/database plus IMAP/SMTP credentials; several advanced channels and features require separate modules

alternatives.name: Zammad
alternatives.desc: A mature team inbox with internal notes and ticket owners; it feels like support software because it is.

facts.install: Deploy the Docker Compose/Portainer stack or install supported Linux packages
facts.dataFormat: Ticket and user data in PostgreSQL, search indexes in Elasticsearch, and attachments/backups in Docker volumes or server storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It feels like support-ticket software rather than Missive's flexible collaborative email and team-chat workspace.
facts.setupBlocker: A comparatively large server and familiarity with Docker/Portainer, PostgreSQL and Elasticsearch

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Starter plan and a personal desktop mail client DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Missive in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, SQLite, IMAP, SMTP, and OAuth where available; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: connect an existing mailbox, index messages locally, combine email with internal comments and assignments for a small team, and send through the account's normal SMTP service.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Support one IMAP and SMTP account with credentials stored only in the OS keychain.
Index headers and message bodies locally with resumable sync and a visible status page.
Implement standards-based threading, folders, labels, archive, snooze, drafts, and search.
Render HTML email in a locked-down sandbox and block remote images by default.
Send multipart messages with attachments and preserve a local copy of every draft.
Add export, local cache reset, account reconnect, diagnostics, and safe logging.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out running a public mail server.
Deliberately leave out shared team inboxes and sales workflows.
Deliberately leave out mobile push services and provider-scale spam filtering.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
